## The notebooks and their documentation

A single-node AI prompt-security lab that runs on one Apple-Silicon
MacBook: a real Kubernetes edge, a real policy gate, a real LLM
application — and a real attack that succeeds when the gate is removed,
and fails when it is in place.

## How to use this index

This page is the table of contents for the lab. Open a notebook from the table,
read the description above each cell, run top to bottom, and continue
with the notebook named in the run-order table. No jumping between directories:
install once ([Installation](installation.qmd)), open this page, read, click.


## What the lab proves, in run order

1. The vulnerability is real — on the gate-free path, the canary leaks
   into the CRM sink (proven by assertion in
   [05_attacks](https://github.com/shsingh/ai-sec-lab/blob/main/notebooks/05_attacks.ipynb)).
2. The defense is layered, cheap-first — four evaluator tiers short-
   circuit from <1 ms keywords to the Laya decision model.
3. The gate holds — every attack category through the edge returns 403
   and the sink gains nothing.
4. The gate is transparent — benign prompts return 200 with real model
   answers.

`nbdev_test --n_workers 0` drives most of the above as an automated
suite; the `tofu apply` and the real-model leak proof are `# slow`
cells, run interactively on first setup ([USAGE.md](usage.qmd) lists
every assertion in order).

## Contents

| Run order | Notebook | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| — | [index](https://github.com/shsingh/ai-sec-lab/blob/main/notebooks/index.ipynb) | this contents page |
| 1 | [00_core](https://github.com/shsingh/ai-sec-lab/blob/main/notebooks/00_core.ipynb) | the shared constants (namespace, images, edge URL, victim URL) + the fail-closed shell helper + the cluster front-door test; every other notebook imports from here |
| 2 | [01_nova_rules](https://github.com/shsingh/ai-sec-lab/blob/main/notebooks/01_nova_rules.ipynb) | the four `.nov` rule files, one per evaluator tier (keywords → semantics → LLM judge → full spectrum), each live-scan tested against real attacks |
| 3 | [02_gate_app](https://github.com/shsingh/ai-sec-lab/blob/main/notebooks/02_gate_app.ipynb) | the FastAPI gate — NOVA's four tiers plus the Laya decision model behind one HTTP surface — and its pre-baked container image |
| 4 | [03_victim](https://github.com/shsingh/ai-sec-lab/blob/main/notebooks/03_victim.ipynb) | Atlas, the deliberately vulnerable support assistant: stealable canary in the system prompt, poisoned order note (indirect injection), CRM sink as exfiltration target |
| 5 | [04_deploy](https://github.com/shsingh/ai-sec-lab/blob/main/notebooks/04_deploy.ipynb) | OpenTofu declares and applies all ten cluster objects: namespace → ConfigMap → gate → victim → Gateway → HTTPRoute, then rollouts and the first edge probe |
| 6 | [05_attacks](https://github.com/shsingh/ai-sec-lab/blob/main/notebooks/05_attacks.ipynb) | the two-path proof — the real leak on the direct path, then the same attack corpus blocked 403 at the edge with the sink untouched, plus the free-play scratchpad for rule iteration |

## How a request flows

```
curl ──▶ NGINX Gateway Fabric (HTTPRoute, :80)
          └─▶ nova-gate pod
                ├─ NOVA: keywords → semantics → LLM judge   (fail closed on any hit → 403 JSON)
                └─ Laya: typed verdict (injection / jailbreak / benign)
                      └─▶ Atlas pod ──▶ real LLM answer (200)
```

Atlas is also reachable from inside the cluster (`atlas:8080`) without
the gate — the unprotected path that makes the two-path proof in
[05_attacks](https://github.com/shsingh/ai-sec-lab/blob/main/notebooks/05_attacks.ipynb) possible.
